title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Manager
tiers.description: A Restricted Person who is a member of Key Management Personnel or otherwise determined by the Board to be a Manager, including any holder of the office of Director, CEO, Executive Director, Group CFO, CIO, Head of Pricing and Structuring, or Group General Counsel and Company Secretary, or an Associate of any of those persons. May Deal only during defined Open Periods rather than outside Closed Periods.

tiers.name: Restricted Person
tiers.description: Every Director, all Employees of any Group member, contractors/consultants/workers/interns as determined by the Company Secretary, and any Associate of such a person. May Deal at any time other than the Closed Periods (unless also a Manager, in which case only during Open Periods).

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Director elected chair of the Board; distinguished from other Directors only for clearance, where the Designated Officer is the Managing Director and Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Director (other than chairperson)
tiers.description: Directors other than the Chair; distinguished only for clearance, where the Designated Officer is the Chair and Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associate
tiers.description: Immediate Family Members (spouse, de facto partner, parent, and any child under 18) of a Restricted Person, and any company, trust or other entity controlled by the Restricted Person or their Immediate Family Members.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, or its delegate (the Chair of the Board and the Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee), may determine additional Open Periods for Managers (3.1(f)) and additional Closed Periods for other Restricted Persons (3.2(c)). The Policy does not state whether such determinations are confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. Security is defined to include securities issued by third parties over the Company's securities, such as derivatives, with no venue limit, so an OTC put/call is a Security and dealing in it is a Deal requiring prior written clearance and compliance with the Open/Closed Period regime.
rules.evidence: means shares or debt securities or any other securities issued by the Company or by third parties over such securities of the Company, such as derivatives

rules.detail: 'Hedging' and 'limiting economic risk' are not used anywhere in the Policy, and there is no separate hedging rule for vested or unvested incentive securities; only the general margin lending/encumbrance/lending-arrangement controls and the general Dealing/clearance regime could incidentally capture a collar.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar arrangement disposing of the economic exposure to Company Securities falls within 'disposing' or 'converting' a Security (which includes derivatives), making it a Dealing requiring pre-dealing clearance; if it grants security over the shares it is also caught by 2.2.
rules.evidence: means any transaction associated with subscribing for, buying, selling, transferring, disposing or converting a Security

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or defined anywhere in the Policy (only trading 'in and out' of Securities of a Short-Term Nature is addressed). A short sale sourced by borrowing OBL shares would separately engage the 2.2(c) restriction on lending arrangements.

Restricted Persons must not engage in any lending arrangements in respect of Company Securities without the prior written consent of a Designated Officer; this is consent-based, not an absolute ban, despite sitting under the 'prohibited at all times' heading.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not, without the prior written consent of a Designated Officer: ... (c) engage in any lending arrangements in respect of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a financial product created over the Company's Securities and so falls within the Security definition (which extends to derivatives), making entry into one a Dealing requiring clearance; a short-dated CFD would also usually be caught by the six-month Short-Term Nature ban.
rules.evidence: means shares or debt securities or any other securities issued by the Company or by third parties over such securities of the Company, such as derivatives

rules.detail: Restricted Persons must not enter into margin loan arrangements in relation to a Dealing in Company Securities without the prior written consent of a Designated Officer.
rules.evidence: enter into any margin loan arrangements in relation to a Dealing in the Company's Securities

rules.detail: Using Company Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, or granting or permitting to exist any encumbrance over them (including in connection with margin loans), requires the prior written consent of a Designated Officer.
rules.evidence: use the Company's Securities as collateral in any financial transactions, or grant or permit to exist any encumbrance over the Company's Securities, including in connection with margin loan arrangements

rules.detail: Section 2.2 operates as a single consent-based secured financing regime covering margin loans, collateral/encumbrance and lending arrangements over Company Securities: none is banned outright, but all require prior written Designated Officer consent, and the Policy states no criteria constraining that discretion.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must not, without the prior written consent of a Designated Officer: (a) enter into any margin loan arrangements in relation to a Dealing in the Company's Securities; (b) use the Company's Securities as collateral in any financial transactions, or grant or permit to exist any encumbrance over the Company's Securities, including in connection with margin loan arrangements; or (c) engage in any lending arrangements in respect of the Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute, consent-free ban on Dealing of a 'Short-Term Nature', defined as trading in and out of Securities within six months (or such other period as the Board determines).
rules.evidence: a Restricted Person must not: (a) Deal in the Company's Securities: (i) where the Dealing is of a Short-Term Nature

exemption_authority: A Designated Officer may grant Prior Written Clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of Company Securities during a Restricted Period for severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances (court order, enforceable undertaking, overriding legal/regulatory requirement, or any other circumstance the Designated Officer deems exceptional), on an application lodged at least 5 Business Days ahead and answered within 2 Business Days, provided the sale is the only reasonable course of action available. There is no equivalent exemption from the Short-Term Nature ban or from the section 2.2 consent requirement for margin loans, encumbrance and lending arrangements, which are separately gated on ordinary Designated Officer consent rather than a hardship-style waiver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must not, without the prior written consent of a Designated Officer: (a) enter into any margin loan arrangements ...; (b) use the Company's Securities as collateral ... or grant or permit to exist any encumbrance ...; or (c) engage in any lending arrangements in respect of the Company's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar, secured on the collared shares, is not banned outright but needs prior written Designated Officer consent, with no stated criteria constraining refusal, so the bank's security interest is contingent on discretionary approval rather than a policy right.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Deal means any transaction associated with subscribing for, buying, selling, transferring, disposing or converting a Security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Moving the collared shares into a custodian, margin or pledge account is itself a Dealing (a 'transfer'), requiring the same prior clearance as the derivative and loan legs and subject to the Open/Closed Period timing restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Manager may only Deal in the Company's Securities during the following 'Open Periods' [post-AGM, post-half-year, post-final results, post-31 March quarterly report, post-disclosure document, or Board-determined].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For Directors and senior executives (the most likely collar counterparties), collar entry, unwind, roll or restructuring is confined to a handful of 4-6 week windows a year rather than any time outside a blackout, materially constraining execution timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approvals once granted are valid for ten (10) Trading Days, unless otherwise notified by the applicable Designated Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar and loan documentation must be completed within the 10 Trading Day clearance window or fresh clearance must be sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if the Restricted Person is a Director they will resign immediately from the Board ... or if the Restricted Person is an Employee they will resign immediately from the Company ... without any claim ... other than for unpaid but due fees or salary.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A second failure to obtain clearance for the collar, loan or any transfer step carries automatic forced resignation/termination, so execution and documentation discipline around this Policy's consent steps is a material counterparty risk for the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a Restricted Person must not directly or indirectly, enter into, trade in, acquire, dispose of, vary or otherwise deal in any Litigation Event Contract ... regardless of whether the relevant litigation ... involves the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This absolute, non-waivable ban is confined to contracts referencing litigation outcomes, not price-referenced equity derivatives, so a standard OBL-share collar is not itself a Litigation Event Contract, but it shows the Board is willing to hard-ban derivative-like products outright with no consent route.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted OBL shares is workable in structure but gated entirely on discretionary written consent, not as of right. The put and call legs are Dealings (Security expressly extends to third-party derivatives with no venue limit) requiring prior written clearance from the applicable Designated Officer (Managing Director and Company Secretary for the Chair; Chair and Company Secretary for other Directors; Company Secretary for other Restricted Persons), valid for only 10 Trading Days, and executable only within a Manager's Open Periods or, for other Restricted Persons, outside the two annual Closed Periods, with no Inside Information held. The loan leg, secured by a charge over the collared shares, falls within section 2.2's consent (not prohibition) regime for margin loans, collateral and encumbrances, and any transfer of the pledged shares into a custodian or margin account is itself a Dealing needing the same clearance. The six-month Short-Term Nature ban is an absolute, consent-free prohibition, so collar tenor should exceed six months. Because approval is discretionary with no stated criteria and a second policy breach triggers mandatory resignation or termination, the bank should treat Designated Officer consent as a condition precedent rather than a formality.
